Survival game workbench

Pick what you want to work in. Create holds the editors for building and tuning things. Game is where the pieces are played.

Create

Editors. Change how something looks or moves and see it straight away.

Character EditorReshape, recolour and re-time a character, then walk and fight with it. Blender EditorThe characters modelled in Blender and rendered to sprites: pick a model and its gear, then walk round the arena or the night forest with it. Creature EditorWild boar, deer, bear, snake, moose and wolf: proportions, features, colours, how they move and how they warn before attacking. Object EditorOne world object at a time: trees, rocks, furniture, machines. Size, shape, surface and colour. Hird EditorThe people who join you: roll a hirdman, tune the stat ranges, traits, jobs, food and the claim stone's reach, and hand it to the game. Item EditorSwords, axes, picks, knives and bows: material, size, sharpness, glow, twist and curl, with a name and a tale. Give them to the game. Song EditorThe game's music, played by its own instruments: the meadow by day and by evening, with a fight layer. Tempo, key, tracks and notes, and export as .mid. Sea EditorBoard a ship at the jetty and sail the archipelago. Four Viking ships, with handling, island sizes and sea distances to tune.

Game

Playable pieces. There is no single game build yet, so each system has its own page.

Combat ArenaFight wolves, boars, snakes and the bear. Art DirectionThe same scene in the old look and the new: Egerkrans’s ink line, Bauer’s light, grain in every fill, cool shadows. The rules as sliders, settings as text, and Use in the game. Light EditorLighting for a flat world: shadows cast by the sun through the day, the colour of the hour, the fire’s light at night, sun rays, a lit rim on every figure, and the trolls’ heads given form. Village EditorThe rules that grow a village: an archetype, a seed, the wealth and the shore; the yard, the longhouse, the houses round it, the fences, the fields and the finds. "Use in the game" hands the numbers over. Gathering EditorChopping, mining and cutting as a small game: the sweet spot, rhythm, trees that fell what they land on, trunks to chop into logs, cracks in rocks, nests, stumps that grow back. Try each, tune it, hand it to the game. Rune EditorThe game started on the big island at a carver’s bench with a ring on your arm and every rune known: try the runes, cut them, change them. Its own save; the real game is untouched. The gameThe first island: chop trees, mine stone, hunt the boar, and keep what you find.
